scenes.title: Serverless Compute (Lambda & Functions)
scenes.narration: Serverless compute like AWS Lambda runs your code in response to events without you managing any servers, scaling automatically and charging only per execution.

scenes.title: Why Serverless Fits Data Work
bullets: You upload only your code, and the provider handles servers, scaling, and patching entirely.
It scales from zero to thousands of parallel runs automatically as events arrive.
You pay per invocation and runtime, so idle functions cost nothing at all.
scenes.narration: With serverless you hand over just your function code, and the platform manages every server underneath. It scales out automatically when many events fire and shrinks back to zero when quiet. Since billing is per invocation, functions that sit idle cost you nothing.

scenes.title: Event-Driven Trigger
scenes.narration: Serverless shines in event-driven pipelines. When a new file lands in object storage, the bucket emits an event that triggers a Lambda function. The function then transforms or routes the data, all without a server waiting around idle. This pattern powers countless lightweight ingestion tasks.

scenes.title: Serverless vs. VMs
scenes.narration: Serverless removes server management entirely and scales down to nothing between events, which is ideal for short bursts of work. Virtual machines keep running and give you full OS control, better suited to long-lived processes. Choosing between them comes down to whether your work is bursty or continuous.

scenes.title: A Simple Lambda Handler
scenes.narration: A Lambda function is just a handler that receives an event and a context. Here the event carries S3 records, so the code loops through each and reads the bucket and key of the new file. From this hook you can kick off validation, transformation, or a downstream load with only a few lines of code.

scenes.text: Serverless functions let you run event-driven data tasks with zero server management and pay only when they execute — perfect for glue between services.
scenes.narration: Serverless compute is ideal for the small, event-triggered tasks that stitch a pipeline together. With no servers to manage and no cost while idle, it is often the cheapest and simplest glue in a data architecture.
